issue_context.title: Remove `Txn(bool)` in `table.MutateContext`
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

For some methods like `Index.Create` or `Index.Delete`, a txn is already provided in the argument:

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/9a7e5cc2f7c433ce238a69a933251a565e089925/pkg/table/index.go#L91-L93

However, because `MutateContext` also provides a `Txn(bool)` method, the coder will be confused about which to choose. Furthur more, in some scenes, the argument `txn` and the return value of `MutateContext.Txn(true)` are not the same, for example in `RecoverIndexExec.backfillIndex`:

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/9a7e5cc2f7c433ce238a69a933251a565e089925/pkg/executor/admin.go#L324-L329

And in `RecoverIndexExec.backfillIndexInTxn`

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/9a7e5cc2f7c433ce238a69a933251a565e089925/pkg/executor/admin.go#L527

A separated txn is created by `kv.RunInNewTxn` not the txn in session.

But in implementation, the `index.create` uses the `ctx.Txn(true)` by mistake:

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/9a7e5cc2f7c433ce238a69a933251a565e089925/pkg/table/tables/index.go#L209-L213

Though there is no bug here because `untouched` is always true, we still need to care about it.

Maybe remove `Txn(bool)` from `MutateContext` is a better choice because then we can only use txn in argument .

review_comments: We should not use `sctx.Txn()` here because it can be different with the txn in argument.
Is there a test covering this?
No, because there is no bug now for `untouched` is always false in DDL reorg and `admin recover index` scene. But it is a potential risk...
